definition: A hindrance of dullness, heaviness, and sinking energy of mind and body.
notes: The project uses sloth and torpor as the default for this hindrance because that is how Dhammarato names it throughout the 2014–2026 talk transcripts (about 110 uses of sloth and torpor, against no uses of dull distraction); the pair name is kept even though the members are governed separately as sluggishness (thīna) and drowsiness (middha); sloth and torpor are recorded as their alternates. It names a sinking and blunting of practice-energy rather than ordinary laziness. Dull distraction, the earlier house default built on the OSF glossary's distraction family, remains the alternate where continuity with earlier OSF material matters. The family label is now hindrance (nīvaraṇa), and the five members are named the way Dhammarato names them. Compounds built on this pair inherit the same name unless a narrower compound record documents an override.
